# astscan 0.1.1

Run AST searches directly from a shell with `--pattern` and `--cypher`.
Use `astscan debug` to check the node kinds and field names before writing a
query. For generated batches, pass a JSON array on stdin with `--rule -`.

```sh
cargo install astscan --version 0.1.1 --locked
demo="$(mktemp -d)"
printf '%s\n' 'console.log("hello");' > "$demo/main.js"
astscan debug "$demo/main.js"
astscan scan -l JavaScript -p 'console.log($ARG)' -- "$demo/main.js"
```

The AST includes a `call_expression`. The search prints one JSON line
with rule ID `pattern-1` and a capture named `ARG` for `"hello"`.

Existing `--rule FILE` commands still accept YAML. In Rust,
`RuleSet::compile` accepts JSON arrays alongside YAML rule documents.
